propositions: Full-suite scheduler load causes git-fetch dribble test to intermittently misclassify valid transfers as stalled due to delayed fixture wake-ups reducing cumulative throughput below promised rate.
Test helper sends fixed rate//10 byte chunks per 0.1-second nominal interval; scheduler delays permanently reduce actual throughput and can cause libcurl to abort during sufficiently long send gaps.

Shared 2-second low-speed window applied to both zero-byte stall controls and above-floor negative controls is too aggressive for variable scheduler latency; production uses intentional 10-second window.

Remedy: extract cumulative bytes-owed calculation into deterministic unit test, keep 2-second window only for zero-byte stall tests, use production 10-second window for one real Git integration check, and replace redundant dribble timing trials with argv configuration proof tests.
